title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote mixes the 1965 manuscript on the Galois theory of motives with recycled typescript sheets. The neighbouring 'pages' are Bourbaki-style drafts on analytic continuation, typed on the other side of the paper, and are unrelated. This page is a short manuscript fragment on the structure of additive (A-linear) categories, preliminary to a tannakian/motivic formalism.

Reading (in modern terms): fix an object X of an A-linear category C and put O = End(X), probably what is meant by the garbled 'Contend(X)'; O may be non-commutative, hence the right modules. Consider objects of the form P ⊗_O X, with P a finitely generated projective right O-module. These are defined as representing Hom_O(P, Hom(X,-)), i.e. as direct summands of X^n. The requirement that such 'tensor products be reasonable' amounts to these objects existing and being 'strict' (well behaved). It implies that the full subcategory generated by X is equivalent, via Y ↦ Hom(X,Y), to a full subcategory of P_d(O) (finitely generated projective right O-modules) containing the object 1 = O_O. Grothendieck asks whether the converse holds and remarks that full faithfulness ('plénitude') is then automatic. That is the Yoneda/Morita statement add(X) ≃ proj(End X).

Next step: for a 'strict' category C, the 'monogenic' full strict subcategories (those generated by one object) form a small filtered system ('cocinant' should be 'filtrant'). C is the inductive limit (union) of this system, since any finitely many objects lie in the subcategory generated by their direct sum.

Conclusion boxed at the bottom: an A-linear category is strict if and only if it is a filtered inductive limit of full subcategories, each equivalent to a full subcategory of some P_d(O) containing O. This is a structural lemma, presumably used to reduce statements about tensor or abelian categories to module categories over endomorphism rings, as in the Tannakian reconstruction from a fibre functor.
errors: The converse ('et inversement ?') needs care. A full subcategory of P_d(O) containing O need not be closed under direct summands or finite sums, so 'strict' must be interpreted as something weaker than idempotent-complete, or the subcategories must be taken to be all of P_d(O). The note leaves this unresolved.
Saying 'plénitude' is automatic is fine for Hom(X,-) restricted to add(X), by Yoneda. It is not automatic for arbitrary objects outside add(X).

ideas.what: The additive subcategory generated by an object X is equivalent to finitely generated projective right modules over End(X).
ideas.where_published: Implicit in tannakian arguments in Saavedra Rivano's thesis (1972), written under Grothendieck's direction

ideas.what: Any (Karoubian) additive category is the filtered union of its monogenic full subcategories.
ideas.modern_name: Filtered colimit of finitely generated (one-object-generated) subcategories
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used e.g. in Deligne, 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Morita/Yoneda bookkeeping, reducing additive categories locally to categories of projective modules over endomorphism rings. It is a routine preliminary for tannakian theory, well known and absorbed into Saavedra and Deligne.
transcription_corrections: 'petit [?] cocinant [?]' should read 'petit [système] filtrant' (small filtered system).
'Contend(X))' is probably 'O = End(X))' or an abbreviation of End(X).
'à une 2-sous-catégorie pleine' should probably read 'à une sous-catégorie pleine'.
'signifie à celle que' is probably 'équivaut à celle que'.
In 'P⊗_O X ... avec P projectif de t.f. sur O)', t.f. = 'type fini'.
